chunks: A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Muhammad ibn Abi Hamza, from one of our companions, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
Leave the Tawaf while you are still desirous of it.

key_terms.تَشْتَهِيهِ: Desiring it / having a strong inclination

ai.seo_question: When should one stop performing Tawaf according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In Shia jurisprudence, this hadith from al-Kafi underscores the principle of *khushu'* (spiritual presence) over mere mechanical completion, suggesting that ending while the heart is still engaged prevents the transition from devotion to burden. Scholars often cite this to encourage worshippers to prioritize the quality of their connection with the Divine during rituals like Tawaf, rather than fixating solely on the numerical count. This approach aligns with the broader Shia emphasis on the inner state (*batin*) complementing the outer form (*zahir*) of worship.
